blocks.content: A ResourceQuota caps the total resource consumption within an entire namespace, preventing any one team or project from consuming far more than its fair share of the shared cluster.
1. A Cap on the Namespace's Total
blocks.text: 1. A Cap on the Namespace's Total

blocks.content: A ResourceQuota sets a ceiling on the sum of everything within a namespace, not any individual object, this is a namespace-wide budget, not a per-Pod restriction.

blocks.alt: A budget for the whole namespace, not any single object within it

blocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-a-quota
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "10"
    requests.memory: 20Gi
    limits.cpu: "20"
    limits.memory: 40Gi

blocks.content: The most common use caps the sum of every Pod's CPU and memory requests and limits (covered later in this module) within the namespace, ensuring one namespace cannot claim more than its allotted share of the cluster's actual resources.

blocks.alt: The combined CPU and memory footprint of everything in the namespace

blocks.content: Beyond raw CPU and memory, a ResourceQuota can also limit how many of a given object type can exist, a maximum number of Pods, Services, or PersistentVolumeClaims, useful for preventing runaway object creation, not just resource consumption.

blocks.alt: Limiting how many objects can exist, not just how much they consume

blocks.content: 4. Preventing One Team From Starving the Rest
blocks.text: 4. Preventing One Team From Starving the Rest

blocks.content: This is exactly the real-world problem ResourceQuota solves, without it, a single team's misconfigured or runaway workload could consume the entire shared cluster's capacity, starving every other team's namespace of the resources they need.

blocks.alt: A shared cluster, protected from any one team consuming it entirely

blocks.content: 5. What Happens When a Quota Would Be Exceeded
blocks.text: 5. What Happens When a Quota Would Be Exceeded

blocks.content: If creating a new Pod would push a namespace's total usage past its ResourceQuota, that Pod creation is simply rejected outright by the API server, this is enforced proactively, at creation time, not discovered after the fact.

blocks.alt: Rejected upfront, at creation time, not discovered as a problem later

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A ResourceQuota caps the total resource consumption and object counts within a whole namespace, protecting a shared cluster from any one team consuming it entirely.
Exceeding a quota rejects new object creation outright, at the API server level, before the problem can ever actually materialize.
